A.explanation: This is too small and comes from misreading the scales, for example using half the wavelength or twice the period in $v = f\lambda$.

B.explanation: This uses $30 \text{ cm}$ as the wavelength, but $30 \text{ cm}$ is only half a cycle on graph 2 from node to node.

D.explanation: With period $T = 0.50 \text{ s}$ and wavelength $\lambda = 60 \text{ cm}$, $v = \lambda / T = 120 \text{ cm s}^{-1}$.

hints: Notice what each axis measures: graph 1 is displacement against time in s at one place, so its repeat length is the period $T$, while graph 2 is displacement against distance in cm at one time, so its repeat length is the wavelength.
Count complete cycles on each graph: graph 1 shows two full oscillations in $1.0 \text{ s}$, and graph 2 repeats from maximum displacement at $0 \text{ cm}$ to the next maximum at $60 \text{ cm}$.
Connect period and wavelength with $v = \lambda / T$ or $v = f\lambda$ with $f = 1/T$, keeping $\lambda$ in $\text{cm}$ to get $v$ in $\text{cm s}^{-1}$.
walkthrough: Identify the period from graph 1. It is a displacement-time graph at a fixed point, so time for one oscillation is the period. Two complete sine waves fit in $1.0 \text{ s}$, so $T = 1.0/2 = 0.50 \text{ s}$.

Identify the wavelength from graph 2. It is a displacement-distance snapshot, so distance for one oscillation is the wavelength. The pattern starts at a crest at $0 \text{ cm}$ and the next identical crest is at $60 \text{ cm}$, so $\lambda = 60 \text{ cm}$.
State the wave equation: $v = f\lambda$ and $f = 1/T$, so $v = \lambda / T$.
Substitute with units: $v = 60 \text{ cm} / 0.50 \text{ s} = 120 \text{ cm s}^{-1}$. The frequency check is $f = 2.0 \text{ Hz}$, so $v = 2.0 \times 60 = 120$.
This matches the $120 \text{ cm s}^{-1}$ value. This is option D
